result:
I'd make it easy for people to say "I was wrong."

Ending poverty or disease would relieve more suffering right away. But I'd pick something upstream, because so many problems persist not because we lack solutions but because changing course means someone has to admit a mistake. Admitting a mistake feels like losing status, so people defend bad policies, stay in feuds, and double down on failing plans long after the evidence has turned.

If updating your beliefs were seen as a sign of strength rather than weakness, politics would be less tribal, science would move faster, institutions would fix their errors sooner, and a lot of personal relationships would go better too. It wouldn't solve everything, but it would make most other problems easier to solve.

What would yours be?
